summary.text: Take \(n=8=2^3\), so \(\Omega(8)=3\) is odd and at least \(3\). In the Möbius sum only the \(H_8\) and \(-H_4\) terms survive, giving \(a(8)=8!(H_8-H_4)=25584>0\), contrary to the predicted negative sign.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
H_n=\sum_{j=1}^n \frac1j
\]
be the \(n\)-th harmonic number. The sequence is characterized by
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}\frac{a(k)}{k!}=H_n.
\]
If we put \(b(k)=a(k)/k!\), this says that \(H_n=\sum_{k\mid n}b(k)\). Möbius inversion therefore gives
\[
b(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d,
\]
and hence
\[
a(n)=n!\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d,
\]
where \(\mu\) is the ordinary Möbius function.

We disprove the proposed equivalence by taking \(n=8\). The positive divisors of \(8\) are
\[
1,2,4,8.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{a(8)}{8!}
 =\mu(8)H_1+\mu(4)H_2+\mu(2)H_4+\mu(1)H_8.
\]
The Möbius values in this expression are
\[
\mu(8)=0,\qquad \mu(4)=0,\qquad \mu(2)=-1,\qquad \mu(1)=1.
\]
Indeed, \(8\) and \(4\) are divisible by the square \(2^2\), so their Möbius values are zero; \(2\) is a product of one distinct prime, so its Möbius value is \(-1\); and by definition \(\mu(1)=1\). Thus
\[
\frac{a(8)}{8!}=H_8-H_4.
\]
The terms through \(1/4\) cancel in this difference, leaving
\[
H_8-H_4=\frac15+\frac16+\frac17+\frac18.
\]
Using the common denominator \(840\), this is
\[
\frac{168+140+120+105}{840}=\frac{533}{840}.
\]
Since \(8!=40320\) and \(40320/840=48\), it follows that
\[
a(8)=40320\cdot\frac{533}{840}=48\cdot533=25584.
\]
In particular, \(a(8)>0\), and therefore the assertion \(a(8)<0\) is false.

On the other hand,
\[
8=2^3.
\]
The function \(\Omega(n)\) counts prime factors with multiplicity, so this factorization gives
\[
\Omega(8)=3.
\]
Thus \(\Omega(8)\) is odd and is at least \(3\). For \(n=8\), therefore, the right-hand side of the conjectured equivalence—“\(\Omega(n)\) is odd and at least \(3\)”—is true, whereas its left-hand side—“\(a(n)<0\)”—is false.

Hence the claimed equivalence does not hold for every positive integer \(n\), and the conjecture is false.
